title: Derived go test -timeout 416s budget plus WARN-ONLY per-package headroom instrument for both CI test legs

scope.primary_deliverable: Replace the unexplained 300s go test -timeout with a derived provisional 416s budget on both the Linux test and Windows test-windows jobs (derivation written into ci.yml with commits e5a325a20/72f9cfeca/8e3927950 named), pin value+derivation with a cihygiene gate test, and ship tools/ci/headroom — a WARN-ONLY per-package headroom reporter with a runtime anti-vacuity guard and package-count floor — built to $RUNNER_TEMP and wired into both legs with go test output and exit code preserved.

any re-running of the test suite by the instrument — it consumes the existing go test output only

executor_contract.note: The executor performs NO git write operations (no add/commit/stash/checkout/branch/reset/clean/push); read-only git (status/diff/show) is fine. The controller builds one commit per milestone, so each milestone must leave the tree green. Mutation checks restore files from /tmp cp backups, never git checkout. Locally: run shell acceptance commands under bash (not zsh; process substitution is used) and export RUNNER_TEMP=${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp} first. The headroom binary and go_test_headroom.log are transient: delete go_test_headroom.log from the repo root after the M3 harness so the worktree stays clean.

milestones.title: tools/ci/headroom instrument: parser, top-N report, WARN-ONLY 75%/90% tiers, anti-vacuity guard and package-count floor, with six unit tests

interface_contract.cli: headroom <logfile|-> <budget-seconds>  (log path FIRST, budget SECOND — all design acceptance examples use this order; '-' reads stdin; usage error exits 2)
interface_contract.exit_codes: 0 = normal (slow packages warn only); 1 = broken instrument — anti-vacuity (non-empty input, 0 records) OR package count below floor minPackages=50; 2 = usage error. These two non-zero paths stay distinct and each has its own unit test.
interface_contract.records: lines 'ok\t<pkg>\t<N.NNN>s' and 'FAIL\t<pkg>\t<N.NNN>s', with optional '(cached)' and '[no tests to run]' suffixes tolerated; duration mandatory; every other line shape yields no record
interface_contract.report: header 'HEADROOM: top 5 slowest packages (budget 416s)', ranked rows 'pkg seconds (pct% of budget)' with ' [go test FAIL]' marker for FAIL lines; sorted seconds desc, pkg name asc tie-break; pct = round(100*seconds/budget)
interface_contract.guard_messages: zero-on-non-empty: '::error:: headroom: parsed 0 packages from non-empty log — parser may be stale'; below floor: '::error:: headroom: parsed <N> packages (< 50) — parser may be stale' (check zero-on-non-empty first; empty log fails via the floor); annotations go to stdout; main() is a thin os.Exit(run(...)) wrapper so exit paths are unit-testable

acceptance_criteria: go test -count=1 ./tools/ci/headroom/ passes with all six tests: TestParseGoTestOutput, TestPercentOfBudget, TestThresholds, TestTopN, TestEmptyParseOnNonEmptyInput, TestPackageCountFloor.

Clean-checkout build + invoke (design objection 4): with no pre-built binary, go build -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/headroom" ./tools/ci/headroom produces an executable; invoking it on a 60-package fixture at 100s/416s prints the HEADROOM report and exits 0.
WARN-ONLY: a fixture with one package at 380s (91% of 416) prints a ::warning:: naming the 90% tier and STILL exits 0 — a slow package is a data point, not a failure.
Anti-vacuity: a garbage non-empty fixture prints '::error:: headroom: parsed 0 packages from non-empty log — parser may be stale' and exits 1.
Floor: a 3-package fixture prints '::error:: headroom: parsed 3 packages (< 50) — parser may be stale' and exits 1.
The tool never invokes go test itself; it only reads the log it is given.
